english.title: Club / institute fail to inform Commission of high turnover bingo period - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[a members' club]_
(B)_[a commercial club]_
(C)_[a miners' welfare institute]_

not holding a bingo operating licence, failed without reasonable excuse to inform the Gambling Commission as soon as reasonably practicable about the beginning of a high turnover bingo period
english.legislation: Contrary to section 275(7) and (8) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 275(2) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that bingo played in the course of the activities of a club or institute in any period of seven days is high turnover bingo if
(a) the aggregate of stakes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, OR
(b) the aggregate of prizes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000.
Section 275(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that a high turnover period beings in relation to a club or institute at the end of a period of seven days during which
(a) the aggregate of stakes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, OR
(b) the aggregate of prizes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000.
(iii) If a club or institute plays high turnover bingo without the appropriate operating licence it will commit an offence under section 33, see offence wording GA05001/H8180.
